SIGHT_HEIGHT_HELP.DIAGRAM: Sketch of a rifle with a riflescope: the sight height H between the bore axis and the scope axis, and the measurable distance A from the top of the scope tube to the bottom of the barrel
SIGHT_HEIGHT_HELP.WHAT: The sight height H is the distance between the bore axis and the axis of the sight.
SIGHT_HEIGHT_HELP.HOW: The axes cannot be measured directly. With calipers, measure the distance A from the top of the scope tube to the bottom of the barrel where the tube is above the barrel, and the barrel diameter at the same spot.
SIGHT_HEIGHT_HELP.FORMULA: H = A − ½ tube diameter − ½ barrel diameter
SIGHT_HEIGHT_HELP.EXAMPLE: Example: A = 70 mm, 30 mm tube, 18 mm barrel → H = 70 − 15 − 9 = 46 mm.

ZEROING.TITLE: Zeroing
ZEROING.INTRO: Calculates the maximum point blank range (MPBR) of the chosen ammunition from the chosen firearm: how far the bullet stays within the vital zone when aiming at its centre, and where it should hit when zeroing.
ZEROING.NO_FIREARMS: You have no firearms yet. Add them on the page
ZEROING.NO_AMMUNITION: You have no ammunition yet. Add it on the page
ZEROING.CALIBER_MISMATCH: The caliber of the ammunition does not match the firearm.
ZEROING.VITAL_ZONE_HINT: Diameter of the area the bullet must hit.
ZEROING.DISTANCE_HINT: Where you zero the rifle, often 35 m.
ZEROING.NO_RANGE: The range cannot be calculated for these values.

MISSING.sight-height: The firearm has no sight height. Add it on the page
MISSING.ballistic-coefficient: The ammunition has no G1 ballistic coefficient. Add it on the page

ZEROING.DISCLAIMER: An estimate for the standard atmosphere (sea level, 15 °C), without wind or spin drift. Factory velocity is measured on a test barrel and is often lower from a shorter one. Always confirm the impacts at the range.
